issues.title: Lévy component moments omit time scaling
issues.failure_explanation: A real-valued Lévy process starts at zero, so the old equalities at t=0 force both hat m and hat v to vanish. They therefore cannot describe the intended nontrivial identically distributed components, and they conflict with the factor t used in special:varconv. The consistent interpretation is that hat m and hat v are unit-time mean and variance rates, giving t hat m and t hat v at time t.
issues.overall_effect: The special-noise assumption, read literally, collapses its intended nontrivial component class and is inconsistent with the subsequent time-scaled estimates and simulations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Assumption ass:SpecialLevyProcess, replace the component identities by E[hat L_{ℓ,m}(t)] = t hat m and E[(hat L_{ℓ,m}(t) − E[hat L_{ℓ,m}(t)])²] = t hat v, thereby identifying hat m and hat v as unit-time rates. No downstream estimate needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The preceding Lévy-process definition, L(0)=0, and the factor t already used in special:varconv uniquely force this reading. The later reasoning already uses time-scaled moments, so inserting the two omitted factors repairs transcription rather than any inference.

issues.title: Malformed Lévy–Khinchin jump integral
issues.failure_explanation: The old equation does not integrate over time and evaluates xi at the terminal time, so it does not provide the process integral used later. The paper defines the random measure as N-tilde(dt,dzeta), and the proof of prop:regul instead uses the distinct object integral_0^t integral_chi xi(s,zeta) N-tilde(ds,dzeta). Thus the stated decomposition does not furnish the required stochastic convolution.
issues.overall_effect: The general Poisson-noise branch of the regularity proposition lacks its stated stochastic-integral input, and the corresponding branch of the spectral weak corollary is consequently unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ass3 by L(t) = W(t) + ∫_0^t∫_χ ξ(s,ζ) Ñ(ds,dζ). Proposition prop:regul and the dependent weak corollary can then retain their existing stochastic-convolution arguments unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old source defines Ñ through its time-space differential and later writes exactly the required double stochastic integral in prop:regul. Thus the missing time integration and the terminal-time argument are uniquely recoverable notation errors, not missing stochastic-analysis work.

issues.title: Malformed real spherical harmonic basis

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The real-valued spherical harmonics form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\S^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For m=-1 the old definition gives both Y_{1,-1} and Y_{2,-1} as the same nonzero function varphi, so the family is not orthogonal. Moreover, applying the displayed spherical Laplacian to this branch gives zero away from the coordinate seam, not -ell(ell+1) times the function. Lemma L:MESol uses the asserted orthonormal eigenbasis to expand the solution and apply Parseval, so its derivation is invalid under the literal definition.
issues.overall_effect: The solution expansion, Sobolev coefficient calculations, spectral approximation, and Euler–Maruyama error analysis all lose their stated orthonormal eigenbasis input.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keeping the old normalized sine branch for m>0, replace the malformed m<0 branch by the normalized complementary branch √2(−1)^m[(2ℓ+1)/(4π)·(ℓ−|m|)!/(ℓ+|m|)!]^{1/2}P_{ℓ,|m|}(cos ϑ)cos(|m|φ). This restores the asserted real orthonormal Laplace eigenbasis, after which all listed expansions and estimates remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The text expressly identifies the family as the standard real spherical harmonics and states its orthonormality and eigenvalue relation. With the already valid positive-m sine branch fixed, those properties force the associated-Legendre cosine branch up to an immaterial sign. Every affected proof uses only the intended basis properties, so the corrupted displayed branch requires no repair of the arguments.

issues.title: Missing test-function moment and regularity restrictions

failure_location.quote: Then, for all test functions~$\varphi$ satisfying \eqref{eq:test_function-reg-poly}

issues.failure_explanation: The prose and corollary claim the doubled weak rate for all polynomial-growth test functions. The proof through prop:regul actually supplies only an L^p moment, so a derivative of degree m is covered only when 2m is no larger than the available moment order, and the desired spatial rate additionally requires rho=eta+1 in the Wiener/independent setting or rho<eta+2/p in the general setting. For a fixed p, an admissible compound-Poisson component can have a finite p-th moment but no 2m-th moment when 2m>p, making the test-function factor used in weakr nonintegrable. Thus the unrestricted old conclusion exceeds its support.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised spectral weak bounds may be undefined or unproved for high-growth test functions and may claim a spatial rate not supplied by the available regularity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the corollary with moment-compatible test functions: for derivative growth of degree m, require the applicable solution, initial-data, and noise moment hypotheses at an order p with 2m≤p. For the doubled Wiener or independent-component rate, take ρ=η+1; in the general Poisson setting require the regularity range supplied by prop:regul, namely ρ<η+2/p (equivalently ρ<η+1/m when p=2m). Assert the existing weak bounds only under these qualifications.
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and uses the existing regularity proposition and weak-error proof, so no global reconstruction is needed. It nevertheless withdraws the natural advertised claim for arbitrary polynomial growth under a fixed finite moment order and restricts the regularity governing the rate. The resulting weak corollary remains recognizably comparable, making the loss limited rather than major.

issues.title: Unjustified eta=-1 endpoint in temporal estimates
issues.failure_explanation: Assumption ass:StrongLevyProcess permits eta=-1 uniformly. At that value the proof chooses mu=min{(eta+1)/2,1}=0 in Peqiii, although prop:AuxExp assumes mu in (0,1]. The same endpoint problem occurs when deriving the h^min{beta,1}=h^0 noise term in Thm:ConvEM2. Thus the cited estimates do not cover the stated endpoint.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal strong and second-moment proofs have a gap at eta=-1; all eta>-1 cases remain covered by the stated auxiliary proposition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle η=−1 separately instead of invoking prop:AuxExp with μ=0. For λ=ℓ(ℓ+1)>0, direct integration and the Euler geometric sum give ∑_j∫|e^{−λ(t_k−s)}−ξ^{k−j+δ}|²ds≤C/λ and the analogous quadrature difference is at most C/λ; the λ=0 mode is exact. Summing these bounds with the H^{−1} moment weights supplies the stated h⁰ terms in Thm:ConvEM and Thm:ConvEM2, while the existing proof covers η>−1.
issues.why_classification: The invocation of an estimate outside its parameter range is a genuine proof gap. At the endpoint, however, the recorded guarantee is only an O(1) bound, and elementary stability and geometric-series estimates establish it locally with no hypothesis, rate, or conclusion lost.

issues.title: Unquantified temporal-error exponent
issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's mean bound contains h^mu but supplies no range or quantifier for mu. The invoked estimates Peqi and Peqvi are stated only for mu in (0,1]. Interpreting the free parameter as unrestricted makes the claim false: for a nonzero deterministic spherical mode with no noise, Euler approximation has a generally first-order error, so the asserted h^mu mean bound cannot hold uniformly for mu>1. The proof therefore establishes only the restricted statement.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal mean and second-moment theorem has an undefined parameter contract and, under an unrestricted reading, overclaims the attainable mean-error order.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bind the free exponent in Thm:ConvEM2 by adding that the two estimates hold for every μ∈(0,1]. No displayed bound or proof step otherwise needs modification.
issues.why_classification: The immediately preceding auxiliary proposition, the preceding temporal theorem, and the proof all give the same unique range μ∈(0,1]. The unbound symbol does not state a well-defined wider rate contract; supplying its source-forced quantifier is a transcriptional scope correction, and the proof already establishes the corrected statement.
